text:
jenny_acme: Hey team — large number of our mobile users are seeing 429s starting ~10:05 UTC after we pushed a promo. Error rate ~8% of requests for a 15m window. App is single-page, lots of background syncs. Anyone seen this pattern?

maria: Sorry you're hitting this, can you paste a few response headers from a 429? Also which region and org id?

jenny_acme: region=us-west-2, org_id=acme-inc, sample 429 response headers we captured: 

x-rate-limit-limit: 1200
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rate-limit-reset: 61
Retry-After: 61
content-type: application/json

Also saw a different batch with: x-rate-limit-limit: 60, x-rate-limit-remaining: 0, x-rate-limit-reset: 5 — not sure why two different limits.

ashok: Two things likely: 1) per-route or per-method short-window RPM (e.g., 60/min) vs account-wide RPM (1200/min). 2) Mobile clients sometimes fan out multiple requests in parallel (background sync + foreground). That explains different headers: one is route-level, one is account-level.

leo: Can you repro with a simple script? If we can reproduce from a single user we can prove client-side burst. Jenny, can you run this from your environment?

jenny_acme: Running now — here's the minimal repro I used (curl loop):

```bash
for i in {1..100}; do 
  curl -s -D - -o /dev/null \  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACME_KEY" \  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \  -d '{"input":"hi"}' \  https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/chat; 
  sleep 0.2;
done
```

After ~30 requests I start seeing 429s with Retry-After: 61.

maria: Perfect repro, thanks. That sleep(0.2) => 5 requests/sec ~300 RPM which can easily exhaust a route limit of 60/min and contribute to the account RPM.

ashok: TL;DR of what we're seeing: short-window per-route limit (60/min) trips first, then account-level RPM kicks in (1200/min), both surface via the headers. Clients that retry aggressively without jitter amplify the spike and risk hitting TPM (tokens/minute/hour) for embedding-heavy workloads.

ratebot: Automated alert: org=acme-inc, rate_limit_events=278 in 15m window, p95 latency rose from 220ms -> 520ms during spike.

leo: Mitigation checklist (short-term):
- Add exponential backoff + full jitter on 429s (start 500ms, max 60s)
- Honor Retry-After header strictly; don't pile immediately after it expires
- Reduce client concurrency (max concurrent inflight requests per device = 2)
- Switch repeated background syncs to coalesced polling (stagger between devices)

maria: Longer-term options:
- Use token-level caching/prefix caching for identical prompts to avoid repeated model invocations
- Batch inputs where possible (server-side aggregation) to reduce requests per user
- Move some non-urgent work to off-peak windows via queueing

jenny_acme: Two questions: 1) Can you increase short-term quota while we patch the client? 2) Why did Retry-After sometimes say 5s and sometimes 61s?

ashok: 1) We can open a temporary quota bump for your account for the promo window — I'll start that process and loop in customer success. 2) 5s is the route-level cooldown (short window) response when you hit an endpoint-specific throttle; 61s is the account-level reset (longer window). They can appear interleaved depending on which limit was hit first for that request.

leo: Also check for the client creating multiple sockets after network flaps — some mobile SDKs retry on every reconnect and reissue queued requests leading to bursts. If you have a device log showing retries after intermittent network, share it.

jenny_acme: We do have an SDK reconnect flow that immediately retries queued requests. We'll add jitter and cap concurrency this morning. Can you do the quota bump? The promo runs for 4 hours from 11:00–15:00 UTC.

maria: Started internal ticket TRE-4521 to request a temporary rate increase for acme-inc for 11:00–15:00 UTC. CS assigned: maria. Please DM me the org_id and expected RPS so I can attach to the request.

ashok: Also posting some troubleshooting commands — check your console logs for aggregated usage:

```bash
# get org usage for last 1h (example)
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_KEY" \  https://console.redwood.example.com/api/v1/orgs/acme-inc/usage?window=1h

# tail 429 logs from our edge (prod)
kubectl logs -n prod gateway-abc -c limiter | grep acme-inc | tail -n 200
```

leo: If you want a durable fix, consider:
- Moving heavy non-interactive calls to a dedicated worker pool with a separate API key and rate limits (segregates traffic)
- Requesting a dedicated capacity slot (Reserved) if this is recurring traffic pattern — reduces noisy neighbor throttles and gives predictable throughput.

jenny_acme: Thanks. We patched the SDK (cap concurrency + jitter) and run a quick load test — redwood 429s dropped from 8% -> 0.2% in our staging stress test. Patch going to prod in 15m.

maria: Great. Follow-up items:
- maria: complete quota bump ticket TRE-4521 (in progress)
- ashok: validate logs & confirm which limit was the hot path (route vs account)
- jenny_acme: deploy SDK update and report back if any residual 429s

ratebot: Note: quota-bump-request TRE-4521 created, state=awaiting-approval, approver=eng-ops.

jenny_acme: One last ask — can you expose per-route rate limit metrics to our console (so we can correlate spikes)? Currently we only see account-level charts.

ashok: Noted. I'll file a feature request FR-1298 to add per-route throttling charts to the org dashboard (will include per-minute and per-hour windows, and sample request traces).

leo: Closing loop — once TRE-4521 is approved I'll confirm the temporary limits and monitor during your promo. Good job catching this quickly — classic client-side burst + no jitter. :thumbsup:

jenny_acme: Thanks everyone — will report back after prod rollout. :pray:
